primary_antecedent.receiving_contribution: Scalar regularization and diffraction antecedent. The complete matrix, actual weak trace, source pairing and elliptic source preparation arguments are independently written here with exact earlier programme proofs. No verbatim source text or figure is reproduced.

source_correspondence: L0 states the actual finite-order local mixed norm, tangential source norm, smooth value datum and whole incoming-support hypothesis. The conclusion is a half-order gain and actual normal-trace regularity, not a full propagation theorem.

L1 proves the trace estimate for unequal tangential orders by Fourier truncation, one-dimensional integration and a Cauchy limit. It identifies the same actual graph trace and supplies the uniform order-minus-three-halves normal bound.

L2 retains the exact regularized equation and every normal/tangential cutoff term. The earlier full-symbol conjugation proof supplies the uniform order-one error and its order-zero Hermitian part. Fixed-parameter H2 inputs and uniform lower source norms are proved before use.

L3 uses separated full microsupports and arbitrarily high composition remainders to control each source pairing. Only tangential adjoints are moved. It does not replace those bounds by a false uniform global L2 source estimate.

L4 reuses both exact characteristic completions and their matrix cancellation. The extra Green boundary pairing for a smooth nonzero value datum is retained with its correct sign and bounded using the lower normal trace. The normal coefficient is adjusted to an exact negative boundary square.

L5 controls the actual incoming norm on its entire support and all regularizer commutators, using a scalar multiplier and the full order-one matrix operator. It does not infer the incoming hypothesis from the principal root alone.

L6 uses the two independent rows, distributional Hilbert limits, complete tangential elliptic remainders and actual normal graph trace commutation. It proves the stated finite-order interior and boundary gains. A common-neighborhood all-order iteration is not assumed.

L7 subtracts the full elliptic normal-cap parametrix from the actual BPL representative. ZE removes all finite-normal source lifts; the finite-normal output cutoff and complete frequency estimates give tangentially smooth forcing. IT gives both actual smooth correction traces. The original Neumann/Robin datum is not converted into a smooth Dirichlet value. Returning to the original energy-b front still needs the correction controlled in that interior norm.

Three complete solutions prove source-norm divergence, sharpness of the lower normal trace exponent and the four-term variable-coefficient cutoff identity. Twenty-six exact checks include a variable noncommuting matrix Green identity and the full incoming commutator expansion.
A formula-spacing typo was corrected and the changed capture re-inspected. Both panels plot exact bounds or exact norm scaling, not numerical propagation.
Twelve local entries bind to 1127 exact earlier entries in 66 maps, including 92 external Lebl proofs.
